Under current plans, the elections will be the last ever to the city council, as it is [[Upcoming structural changes to local government in England|planned to be abolished]] in 2028 and replaced with a [[Unitary authorities of England|unitary authority]]. Elections will be held in 2027 to its replacement authority.{{cite web |title=Timeline |url=https://exeter.gov.uk/council-and-democracy/council-information/local-government-reorganisation/timeline/ |publisher=[[Exeter City Council]] |access-date=14 March 2026}} The elections were initially cancelled alongside others to 29 other authorities similarly planned to be replaced, however in February 2026 it was announced that the elections would go ahead as normal following filings by [[Reform UK]] for [[Judicial review in English law|judicial review]] of the cancellation.{{cite news |last1=Redfern |first1=Martin |title=Exeter local elections to go ahead in May after government cancellation U-turn |url=https://exeterobserver.org/2026/02/16/exeter-local-elections-go-ahead-may-government-cancellation-u-turn-secretary-of-state-steve-reed-withdraws-decision-following-legal-advice-reform-uk-high-court-challenge-city-council-leader-phil-bialyk-electoral-oblivion/ |access-date=14 March 2026 |work=Exeter Observer |date=16 February 2026}} ==Summary== === Council composition === {| class="wikitable" |- ! colspan="3" | After 2024 election ! colspan="3" | Before 2026 election |- ! colspan="2" | Party !
